newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel medical technology exports show sharp rise.
newsitem.headline: Israel medical technology exports show sharp rise.

text.p: Israeli exports of medical electronic equipment have been growing 21-25 percent annually in the last few years and the pace continued in the first quarter of 1997, the Industry and Trade Ministry said on Wednesday.

It said exports of medical electronics grew 24.3 percent in 1996 to $371 million and another 21 percent in the first quarter of 1997 to $92.1 million. Three-quarters of exports were destined for the United States and Europe, it said.
Hilda Gutman, who heads the ministry's high technology division, attributed the growth to pressure in the U.S. and Europe to cut health spending by reducing hospital stays.

Much of the advanced medical equipment developed in Israel is used to computerise and integrate medical procedures, she said in a statement. Israeli companies were also focusing on computerising medical-administrative functions, another growth area, she added.
